headline: Bond volatility finally cracked — MOVE -7.4% — and every rate-crushed asset ripped, but the levels that did the damage are still there: 10y 5.27%, mortgage 7.28% at a 52-week high, breadth at the 4th percentile.
summary: The reprieve is real but narrow. MOVE fell 7.4% to 105.2, its first meaningful break after sitting at the most extreme z-score on the board (now 2.40, acceleration 1.58, down from near-3 yesterday). The whole curve came in: 2y -5bp to 4.79%, 5y -3bp to 5.03%, 10y -4bp to 5.27%, 30y -2bp to 5.64%, and the 10-year real yield -4bp to 2.91%. The rates composite improved from -85 to -80. That one-day rebate paid out exactly where you'd expect: XLU +3.0%, XLRE +1.1%, ITB +1.6%, XHB +1.1%, HD +2.0%, DHI +2.6%, and a violent squeeze in power — CEG +12.2%, VST +10.8%, GEV +4.0%, NLR +5.5%, URA +4.0% — in groups that were sitting at the 11th-13th percentile of 52 weeks. Nothing structural changed. The 10y is still at the 97th percentile and +49bp on the month, the 30y at the 98th, the 30-year mortgage at 7.28% is at the 100th percentile and +62bp on the month with acceleration 1.27, and the 10y real yield still carries z=1.88 with acceleration 1.35. A 4bp day does not fix a 49bp month.

The index keeps printing highs on a hollowing base. SPX +0.6% to 7,818.9 at the 100th percentile and 8.0% above its 200-day; NDX +0.5%, +5.7% on the month. Underneath, RSP/SPY sits at the 3.9th percentile of 52 weeks (z=-1.87, acceleration -1.23), IWM/SPY fell another 1.3% today to -6.0% on the month, RUT -0.6% against SPX +0.6%, and transports and retail relative to the S&P are both at the 0th percentile. Breadth composite -14, risk regime -12 — worse than yesterday's -8 even as bonds eased. And the vol complex is paying less and less for the privilege of hedging it: VIX 15.01 (8.8th percentile), VIX3M 17.64 (1.9th percentile), SKEW -6.8% on the month with acceleration -1.90. Bond vol in the 83rd percentile with z=2.4 while equity tails get cheaper every day is still the single most unstable pair on this page.

Leadership rotated hard within the winners. Semis took the day off — SMH -0.2%, SOXX flat, TSM -0.7%, ASML -1.4%, MU -1.7% — while software and cyber carried it: IGV +1.3% and +5.6% on the week, CIBR +2.0% to a fresh 52-week high (+14.3% on the month, acceleration 1.77), AVGO +3.7%, AMD +2.8%. IGV/SMH +1.5% on the day is the first crack in the semis-only tape. The speculative tail gave back: ARKK -2.5%, BTC -0.3%, COIN -1.3%, and biotech broke outright — XBI -3.4%, IBB -2.3% with acceleration -1.77. Meanwhile yesterday's crude relief reversed: Brent +0.7% to 101.07 and now +5.0% on the month, +36.3% on three, oil/gold +4.9% on the month. Only RBOB cooperated, -3.8% on the day and -2.8% on the month, which is the lone genuine consumer and breakeven offset — breakevens are inert at 2.36-2.37% with 5y acceleration -0.61.

Credit remains the reason this is a rotation and not a regime break. HYG +0.4%, HYG/IEF at the 99th percentile and +1.1% on the month, BKLN at the 95th, credit composite 42. The damage is discount rate, not default. But the casualty list is lengthening in the same places: financials are in open liquidation into earnings season (XLF -6.7% on the month with -8.0% relative strength, GS z=-1.97 and -13.6%, BX -16.7%, IAI -9.3% with z=-1.77, KBE -7.3%), consumer bellwethers are at the floor (MCD at the 1.5th percentile, NKE at the 2nd, HD at the 5.5th, NFLX at the 2.9th), and the precious-metals unwind is accelerating downward (gold -6.4% on the month z=-1.58, silver -6.7%, GDX -11.1% with acceleration -2.04, GDX/gold acceleration -2.06). FX is bifurcating EM: USDBRL -4.6% on the day to 4.98 and Brazil at a 52-week high (EWZ +17.9% on the week), while USDMXN is the new stress point at +6.2% on the month with z=2.38 and acceleration 2.02, and USDINR at the 94th percentile. DXY -0.3% today but still z=1.35 with acceleration 1.23.

good.text: Bond volatility finally broke: MOVE -7.4% to 105.2, the first real decompression after weeks at the most extreme z-score in the digest; the whole curve rallied 2-5bp and the rates composite improved from -85 to -80.

Credit refuses to confirm any of the bond-market stress: HYG +0.4%, HYG/IEF at the 99th percentile of 52 weeks, BKLN at the 95th, credit composite +42. This is a discount-rate shock, not a default cycle.

The growth signal inside commodities is still positive: copper +1.0% to 6.654 at the 92nd percentile, copper/gold +7.7% on the month (z=1.11, acceleration 1.32) at the 98th percentile — the opposite of a recession print.

Non-US leadership broadened to Asia and Brazil: Nikkei +2.4% (+7.6% on the month, z=1.11), Taiwan +2.5% at the 100th percentile, EWJ and EWT at 52-week highs, and USDBRL -4.6% on the day with EWZ +17.9% on the week.
Capitulated power and electrification names squeezed violently off the floor: CEG +12.2%, VST +10.8%, GEV +4.0%, NLR +5.5% from the 11th percentile, ETN +2.9% with acceleration 1.41.
Leadership is widening inside tech rather than narrowing: CIBR +2.0% to a 52-week high (+14.3% on the month, acceleration 1.77), IGV +5.6% on the week, IGV/SMH +1.5% on the day after a -4.7% month.

bad.text: The level of rates is unchanged in any way that matters: 10y 5.27% at the 97th percentile and +49bp on the month, 30y 5.64% at the 98th, 5y 5.03% at the 96th, 10y real 2.91% with z=1.88 and acceleration 1.35. Rates composite -80 is still the worst number on the board.

Housing finance is at an extreme: the 30-year mortgage at 7.28% is at the 100th percentile, +62bp on the month with acceleration 1.27. Today's ITB +1.6% and HD +2.0% bounce is a rate blink, not a thaw — ITB is at the 5.9th percentile and XHB/SPY at the 1.3th.

Breadth deteriorated again under a record index: RSP/SPY at the 3.9th percentile (z=-1.87), IWM/SPY -1.3% on the day to -6.0% on the month, RUT -0.6% against SPX +0.6%, transports/S&P and retail/S&P both at the 0th percentile.

Hedges keep getting cheaper into the thinnest tape of the year: VIX 15.01 at the 8.8th percentile, VIX3M 17.64 at the 1.9th, SKEW -6.8% on the month with acceleration -1.90, while MOVE still carries z=2.40.

Yesterday's crude relief reversed: Brent +0.7% back to 101.07, now +5.0% on the month and +36.3% on three, oil/gold +4.9% on the month. The inflation composite at -29 and breakevens stuck at 2.36% leave no room for an energy re-acceleration.

Financials are still being liquidated into earnings season and biotech just broke: XLF -6.7% on the month (-8.0% relative), GS z=-1.97, BX -16.7%, IAI z=-1.77, KBE -7.3%; XBI -3.4% on the day and IBB acceleration -1.77.

trades.name: Short US housing (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB into the bounce: mortgage 7.28% at a 52wk high
trades.expr: Short ITB outright or buy 2-3 month ITB puts ~5% OTM; cleaner paired against long XLK or SPY for beta-neutrality.
trades.thesis: Affordability is at the worst level in the series: the 30-year mortgage at 7.28% is at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks and +62bp on the month with acceleration 1.27. ITB sits at the 5.9th percentile and 9.7% below its 200-day; XHB/SPY is at the 1.3th. A 4bp dip in the 10y does nothing for the primary mortgage rate and nothing for spring order books.
trades.trigger: ITB +1.6%, XHB +1.1%, DHI +2.6% and HD +2.0% today on a one-day bond rally — the first liquid bounce to sell since the mortgage rate made its high.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back below 6.90% or 10y sustained under 5.00%, or ITB reclaiming its 200-day (a ~10% rally).
trades.target: ITB -8 to -10% from spot; XHB/SPY making new lows below the current 1.3th percentile.

trades.name: Long equity tails vs cheap vol
trades.line: Buy SPX downside: VIX 15.0, VIX3M at the 2nd percentile
trades.expr: Buy Dec/Jan SPY 5-7% OTM put spreads funded by selling a 1-month 2% OTM put, or Nov/Dec VIX 20/30 call spreads. Term structure at 0.851 makes calendars cheap.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for a tape that no longer exists underneath. SPX is at the 100th percentile and 8.0% above its 200-day while RSP/SPY is at the 3.9th percentile and IWM/SPY is making new relative lows. MOVE at z=2.40 with the 10y at 5.27% says the rate regime hasn't resolved; VIX3M at the 1.9th percentile and SKEW with acceleration -1.90 say nobody is paying for that risk.
trades.trigger: VIX -3.3% to 15.01 and VIX3M -2.0% to 17.64 on the same day the breadth ratios deteriorated again and biotech fell 3.4%.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY turning up through their 1-month highs with VIX3M above 20 — i.e. a real broadening that validates the index.
trades.target: VIX 22-25 / SPX -6% on any re-acceleration in 10y yields above 5.40%.

trades.name: Long copper miners vs short gold miners
trades.line: Long COPX / short GDX: copper-gold at the 98th percentile
trades.expr: Long COPX, short GDX, dollar-neutral. Alternative single-name version: long FCX vs short NEM.
trades.thesis: The metals complex is splitting. Copper is +1.0% on the day, +7.8% on three months, at the 92nd percentile, and copper/gold is +7.7% on the month with acceleration 1.32 at the 98th percentile. Gold is -6.4% on the month with z=-1.58 and the miners are unwinding faster than the metal: GDX -11.1% on the month with acceleration -2.04, GDX/gold acceleration -2.06. Falling real-rate hedging demand hurts the gold trade; electrification demand supports the copper trade.
trades.trigger: Today's divergence: COPX -0.1% versus GDX +0.9% as gold bounced 0.8%, giving a better entry price on the short leg after a -11% month.
trades.stop: Copper/gold back below its 200-day (a ~17% move) or gold reclaiming 4,450 with GDX/gold turning up.
trades.target: +10-12% on the spread over a quarter.

trades.name: Long USD/MXN
trades.line: Long USDMXN on the -1.1% dip: z=2.38, acceleration 2.02
trades.expr: Spot/forward long USDMXN at 17.97, or 3-month USD calls/MXN puts with a 18.60 strike. Size 1x; carry is against you.
trades.thesis: The peso is the new pressure point in EM FX. USDMXN is +6.2% on the month with z=2.38 and acceleration 2.02, trend turning up and 3.1% above its 200-day — the most stretched FX move in the digest, bigger than the CAD break. With DXY still z=1.35 (acceleration 1.23), USDINR at the 94th percentile and EEM/SPY acceleration -1.2, a carry trade with crowded positioning and a bill rate at 4.21% in the US has a long way to unwind.
trades.trigger: USDMXN -1.1% today gives entry inside the trend, and EWW -5.1% on the month with MXX rolling over says the local equity bid is gone too.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.45 (below its 200-day), or DXY breaking below 100.50.

trades.name: Long cybersecurity (CIBR)
trades.expr: Long CIBR outright, or long CIBR / short QQQ to isolate the relative leg. Buy pullbacks toward the 20-day; do not chase above +3% from spot.
trades.thesis: This is the cleanest accelerating uptrend on the page that isn't a semiconductor. CIBR is +2.0% on the day, +14.3% on the month, +51.7% YTD, at the 100th percentile with acceleration 1.77 and relative strength of +12.7% (1m) and +12.3% (3m) versus the S&P. With semis stalling today (SMH -0.2%, TSM -0.7%, MU -1.7%) and IGV/SMH +1.5%, software-adjacent spend is where the tech bid is rotating.
trades.trigger: New 52-week high today while SMH and SOXX were flat-to-down, and IGV +5.6% on the week — leadership is handing off within tech, not leaving it.
trades.stop: CIBR losing its 20-day and relative strength versus the S&P turning down (a ~7% drawdown from spot).
trades.target: +12-15%, extension of the current 34.7% premium to the 200-day being worked off by time, not price.

trades.name: Long nuclear/power rebound (NLR)
trades.line: Long NLR after the squeeze: CEG +12%, VST +11% in one day
trades.expr: Long NLR with a tight stop; higher-beta expression via CEG or VST, higher-quality via GEV or ETN. Half size — this is a mean-reversion trade in a downtrend.
trades.thesis: The power complex capitulated into October — NLR -8.8% on the month at the 10.9th percentile and 15.1% below its 200-day, URA -9.2%, CEG flat on the month after a -14.6% year. Today's move was not a drift: CEG +12.2%, VST +10.8%, NLR +5.5%, GEV +4.0%, URA +4.0%. With GRID turning up (acceleration 0.80) and ETN acceleration 1.41, the underlying electricity-demand trade never broke — the financing cost did, and bond vol just cracked lower.
trades.trigger: MOVE -7.4% and 10y -4bp on the same session that produced double-digit single-day gains in the two largest IPPs; NLR week +5.1% off the 11th percentile.
trades.stop: NLR back below today's open / the prior week's low, or 10y above 5.40% which re-kills long-duration power capex.
trades.target: NLR closing half its 15% gap to the 200-day; CEG back to 340.

trades.name: Long S&P vs short Russell 2000
trades.line: Long SPY / short IWM: IWM/SPY -6% on the month, new lows
trades.expr: Long SPY, short IWM, dollar-neutral, ~1:1 notional. Or sell IWM call spreads against long SPY.
trades.thesis: Small caps need lower front-end rates and better credit access; they are getting neither. The 3-month bill is +30bp on the month to 4.21% at the 89th percentile and the 2-year is +42bp — the policy curve is pricing tightening, not easing. IWM/SPY is -6.0% on the month with z=-1.66, down 1.3% today, and regional banks (the Russell's largest financing channel) are at the 20th percentile relative to the S&P with KRE/SPY -7.7% on the month.
trades.trigger: Today's split: SPX +0.6% and NDX +0.5% versus RUT -0.6%, on a day when yields fell — small caps failed to take the rate relief.
trades.stop: IWM/SPY back above 0.372 (reclaiming the 1-month range) or the 2-year breaking below 4.50%.
trades.target: -5% on the ratio from 0.3611 toward the 2025 lows.
